APIT: LLM-powered API test generation as an AI capstone.

A capstone project that analyzes API documentation and generates structured API test cases using controlled data synthesis, LoRA fine-tuning, RAG, and automated evaluation.

Open capstone PDF Back to projects
Context

The capstone targets the Testing & Integration phase of SDLC.

APIT is positioned as an intelligent QA enhancement: it reads standardized API documentation, defines test scope, generates structured test cases, executes them, and reports pass/fail/exception outcomes through a dashboard.

The gap is clear: execution tools such as Postman, JMeter, RestAssured, PyTest, and Newman are useful, but they still depend heavily on manually designed test cases and do not solve intelligent generation by themselves.

My role

System Architecture Designer.

The project document records my role as the system architecture designer, responsible for designing the required system and optimizing system performance. In portfolio terms, this should be framed as system design, workflow design, and QA-domain contribution rather than claiming every model/data task individually.

Pipeline

From API docs to evaluated test cases.

Document preprocessingStandardize API docs from OpenAPI, Swagger, PDF, or structured text.
Test scopeSelect requirements, endpoints, and value/risk boundaries for generation.
LLM generationFine-tuned model + RAG generates structured test cases and reasoning.
Execution/reportRun requests, classify pass/fail/exception, and present results.
Data and model

Controlled synthetic data and small-model adaptation.

The dataset strategy is one of the strongest parts of the project: manually written realistic API documents were distilled into prompts, used to generate controlled API documentation, and then converted into desired test-case outputs with reasoning.

The resulting dataset contained 1,258 samples with an approximately 8:1:1 train/validation/test split and bilingual English/Vietnamese coverage. Qwen-2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B were fine-tuned with LoRA/4-bit training under identical hyperparameters.

Evaluation

Structured output quality was measured, not guessed.

APIT evaluated generated test cases with reference-based precision, recall, and F1. Matching used fuzzy string similarity, numeric tolerance, exact matching for categorical fields, and handling for malformed JSON outputs.

The project also evaluated reasoning quality with logical validity, coherence, and groundedness, which maps well to the Agentic QA direction.

Result

Qwen-2.5-3B LoRA achieved 0.655 macro-F1 on structured API test generation, outperforming the Llama-3.2-3B LoRA baseline under the same setup.
